name: macd_trend_continuation_v71
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY's intraday price action often features 3-8 minute pullbacks within a directional move — caused by profit-taking from early participants or brief counter-flow from hedging algorithms. During these pullbacks, short-term momentum (measured over 2 minutes) turns negative while medium-term momentum (measured over 5 minutes) remains positive. The MACD crossover detects the exact moment when the pullback ends and the original trend resumes: the 2-minute EMA stops falling and crosses back above the 5-minute EMA, meaning short-term flow has re-aligned with the broader direction. Critically, the original MACD strategy requires the MACD line to be below zero for bullish crossovers — this means momentum was genuinely NEGATIVE (not just slowing), and is NOW turning positive. This is a reversal-within-trend signal, which has higher follow-through than a simple 'momentum acceleration' signal because it catches the compressed spring of a pullback unwinding. On NIFTY specifically, these trend-resumption points often coincide with institutional TWAP algorithms restarting their buying after pausing during the pullback, creating a confluence of algorithmic and discretionary flow in the same direction. We enter on the crossover and target the first 30-90 seconds of the resumption move before the next micro-pullback begins.

indicators.name: trend_ema_180
indicators.purpose: 15-minute EMA serves as the trend direction filter, replacing the original EMA(50) on 15-min bars (which covered ~12.5 hours or 1.5 trading days). For 30-90 second holds on NIFTY, we need a trend that is relevant to the CURRENT session's direction, not a multi-day trend. 15 minutes (180 bars) captures the dominant intraday move direction while being responsive enough to flip when NIFTY reverses mid-session. A 30-minute EMA was too slow — it often stayed bullish well into a session reversal.

indicators.name: macd_line
indicators.purpose: MACD line: 2-minute EMA minus 5-minute EMA. The original MACD(12,26,9) on 15-min bars compared 3-hour vs 6.5-hour momentum — far too slow for our holding period. The core MACD insight is detecting when short-term momentum ACCELERATES relative to medium-term. On NIFTY at 5s, micro-pullbacks within trends last 2-5 minutes, so the fast EMA (24 bars = 2 min) captures the pullback momentum while the slow EMA (60 bars = 5 min) captures the trend momentum. When the pullback ends, the 2-min EMA crosses back above the 5-min EMA. These specific periods were chosen because NIFTY's institutional TWAP algorithms typically operate on 3-5 minute cycles, creating predictable pullback rhythms.

indicators.name: macd_signal
indicators.purpose: Signal line: 90-second EMA of the MACD line. The original's 9-bar signal on 15-min (2.25 hours) smoothed over an extremely long period. For 5s NIFTY data, 18 bars = 90 seconds provides enough smoothing to prevent whipsaw crossovers from single-bar noise spikes, while being fast enough to generate the signal within the first 15-30 seconds of a genuine trend resumption. Shorter (9-12 bars) produced too many false crossovers during NIFTY's choppy intraday phases.

indicators.name: macd_histogram
indicators.purpose: Histogram measures the GAP between MACD line and signal. Used to confirm the crossover has conviction — a barely-crossing MACD (histogram near zero) often whipsaws back immediately. We require the histogram to be accelerating (current > previous bar) to filter out weak crossovers.

indicators.name: trend_slope
indicators.purpose: 3-minute slope of the trend EMA in basis points. Ensures the underlying trend is actively progressing, not stalling. A flat trend_ema_180 could be above price purely from earlier momentum — the slope confirms ongoing directional pressure. Requires > 0.3 bps for bullish (NIFTY rising ~0.7 points/minute).

conditions: close > trend_ema_180 (NIFTY is above 15-minute EMA — session is trending bullish)
trend_slope > 0.3 (uptrend is actively advancing, not coasting)
CROSSOVER(macd_line, macd_signal) (2-min momentum crossing above 5-min momentum — pullback ending)
macd_line < 0 at crossover or was < 0 within last 6 bars (momentum was genuinely negative — this is a reversal from pullback, not just continuation acceleration)
buy_ce.confirmation: macd_histogram increasing for 2 consecutive bars after crossover — confirms the crossover has momentum, not just a touch-and-retrace

conditions: CROSSUNDER(macd_line, macd_signal) (2-min momentum crossing below 5-min — bounce ending)
macd_line > 0 at crossover or was > 0 within last 6 bars (momentum was positive — bounce is reversing back into downtrend)
buy_pe.confirmation: macd_histogram decreasing for 2 consecutive bars after crossover

exit.stop_rationale: MACD crossover entries on NIFTY carry the risk that the pullback resumes immediately after the false crossover — typical NIFTY whipsaw after a failed crossover is 5-12 spot points (2.5-6 option points). A 4-point stop is tight because trend-resumption signals should work IMMEDIATELY if the thesis is correct — if NIFTY moves 8 spot points against us after a bullish MACD cross, the pullback was deeper than expected and will likely test lower levels. The tight stop keeps the risk-reward favorable given the aggressive 12-point target.
exit.target_rationale: The original strategy had a very aggressive 21xATR target. The insight was correct — trend-resumption moves have large potential because they ride the primary trend. On NIFTY, when a 3-5 minute pullback ends and the trend resumes, the next leg typically covers 15-35 spot points in 1-3 minutes (7-17 option points). Target of 12 points captures the middle of this range, yielding an aggressive 1:3 risk-reward. This is deliberately asymmetric — win rate will be lower (~38%) but winners will be large enough to compensate. This preserves the original strategy's philosophy of letting trend trades run.

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 13-24 — below 13, NIFTY trends weakly and MACD crossovers lack follow-through; above 24, volatility is too choppy and pullbacks are violent enough to trigger repeated false crossovers
filters.time_filter: No trades before 09:30 (need 15 min of data for EMA and MACD to initialize). No trades after 14:30 — trend-following loses reliability as end-of-day position flattening creates counter-trend noise.
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is aggregated and noisy; MACD on price directly captures the momentum shift
filters.trend_filter: trend_ema_180 and trend_slope serve as the primary trend filter — only trade crossovers aligned with the dominant intraday trend
filters.spread_filter: skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2 points

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — MACD is one of the most widely-used indicators, but the specific parameterization (24/60/18) tuned to NIFTY's TWAP pullback rhythms and the 'MACD line below zero' reversal filter are less crowded

adaptation_notes: Four key changes from the original MACD(12,26,9) trend strategy: (1) MACD periods changed from 12/26/9 on 15-min to 24/60/18 on 5s. This is NOT a blind 12x scaling (which would give 144/312/108 — absurdly long). The original detected 3-hour vs 6.5-hour momentum differentials, which is irrelevant for 30-90 second holds. Instead, the new periods (2min/5min/90s) are calibrated to NIFTY's actual intraday pullback duration: institutional TWAP algorithms create 3-5 minute pullback cycles, so the fast EMA (2 min) captures the pullback while the slow EMA (5 min) holds the trend direction. (2) EMA(50) trend filter on 15-min (12.5 hours) replaced with EMA(180) = 15 minutes plus slope confirmation. Multi-day trend is irrelevant for sub-minute holds. (3) Stop changed from 1.5xATR to 4 option points. ATR-based stops on spot don't translate to option stops due to delta/gamma effects. 4 points = ~8 spot points at delta 0.5, which is the maximum a NIFTY MACD crossover should move against you before invalidation. (4) Target reduced from 21xATR (which implied multi-hour holds) to 12 points — still aggressive at 1:3 R:R, preserving the original's asymmetric payoff structure but calibrated to NIFTY's actual trend-resumption leg sizes of 15-35 spot points.
weaknesses: MACD is inherently lagging — by the time the 2-min EMA crosses the 5-min EMA, the first 5-10 spot points of the resumption move may already be gone, reducing the remaining reward
In choppy, range-bound NIFTY sessions (which occur 30-40% of trading days), MACD generates repeated whipsaw crossovers that each lose the 4-point stop
The aggressive 12-point target means many trades that move 6-8 points in our favor will reverse and hit the stop or time out — the opportunity cost of missed partial profits is significant
On days with heavy options expiry flow (Thursdays), NIFTY's trend patterns become distorted by gamma hedging, and the MACD's momentum assumptions break down
Low win rate (~38%) produces psychological pressure and long losing streaks — 5-7 consecutive losers are expected monthly
